$comment: Riftlight, Wandering Sky strand middle (docs/campaigns/continental-rift/arc.md, whale-road; design note nodes/whale-road.md). Rewritten in November 2026. Question: why are the whales circling, and how do we let them go? Keeper Juniper carries it into the-island-due-back; Lady Olivia appears with Pip and offers her shortcut, which the party takes or refuses on the campaign map (rift action olivia/guide on whales-to-coast). Sets whales_guided only on the gentle ending, and sky_followup_promised true or false on every path.
title: The Whales' Turning Place

plate.narration: Above a grassy island, cloud whales turn through the mist. Their long fins move slowly in the open sky. Below them, a broad green landing waits between the clouds.

goal.text: Why are the whales circling, and how do we let them go?

steps.label: Find what turns the whales back
Lead one whale out the slow way

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny and a little spooky, with real consequences. Short sentences. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel. The whales are gentle, immense and tired, never enemies or mounts. Nobody is lectured about which way is right.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Keeper Juniper: Keeper Juniper, the kitsune island keeper (she/her). Brisk, warm and a little bossy; talks to the whales like old aunties and calls each by name. Knits one row of a scarf for every circle they swim. Wants the whales home and the island due back safely in.
npcVoices.Lady Olivia: Lady Olivia, unicorn Riftseeker (she/her). Bright, kind about the whales, a little too sure. Right that the openings are linked and that the pull will get worse; wants to prove the openings can be used. Hates waiting.
npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: Young manticore scout (he/him). Eager, notebook always out, spoon behind his ear, quotes "Lady Olivia says..." and wants to impress her. Counts pulses out loud. Kind underneath; notices when the whales are sad.

arrive.narration: Past the last stepping island, the sky opens into a wide bowl of mist. Cloud whales swim in it, each one longer than a street, singing low. Round and round they go. On a grassy island, a kitsune sits knitting a scarf longer than she is. "Keeper Juniper," she says. "One row for every circle the whales swim. Forty-one rows. That is far too much scarf." She points a needle at the whales. "Why are they circling? And how do we let them go? Help me find out."

low_pass.narration: A whale swings low to look at you. Its belly brushes the grass, and the whole island tips like a plate of peas. Juniper hugs her knitting. "That's Hiccup, the little one. He's nosy. Hold on to something!" Her ball of yarn starts to roll.

check_posts.narration: The tether posts are old and thick and furry with moss. The grass under your boots starts to slide.
check_posts.prompt: Hug a tether post and hang on while the island tips

onSuccess.narration: You hang on like a burr on a sock. The island rocks back level, and you never let go.

onFailure.narration: Your arms slip. You roll down the grass and land with a splash in Juniper's duck pond. The ducks leave, offended.

check_yarn.narration: The yarn bounces down the tilting grass toward the edge, trailing forty-one rows of scarf behind it.
check_yarn.prompt: Chase the rolling yarn before it bounces off the edge

onSuccess.narration: You snatch it one hop from the edge. Juniper kisses the yarn. Then she kisses the top of your head, which is worse.

onFailure.narration: You dive and miss, and slide on your tummy across the grass. The yarn bounces off into the sky. Juniper reels it back, row by row. "Forty-one. Or forty. Oh, I've lost count."

check_fly.narration: Up close, Hiccup is as big as a barn and as soft as a pillow. He keeps turning to look at you, which makes a lot of wind.
check_fly.prompt: Fly level with Hiccup without getting bumped

onSuccess.narration: You flap along beside him. Hiccup hiccups a tiny cloud right in your face, then rolls back up, and the island rocks level. "He likes you," says Juniper. "He never likes anyone."

onFailure.narration: Hiccup turns to say hello and bumps you with his nose. You tumble back down onto the grass, dizzy and damp. "He likes you," says Juniper. "Too much."

whale_eye.narration: Behind Hiccup comes a whale so big she blocks the sun. Her eye slides past, kind and very tired. "Auntie Billow," says Juniper. "She leads. Whales find their way by singing. And they always swim ahead of the island due back, an old island my people have waited on for a hundred years. When it comes, the whales show us where." She sighs. "Lost whales, lost island."

turn_watch.narration: Every circle, the whales swim to the far end of the bowl. There they slow, listen, and turn back. "Something out there turns them," says Juniper. "I can't leave my whales to go and look. Will you?" How will you find out what turns them?

choices.label: Lie in the grass and listen
Cross the rope walk to the far rock

check_listen.narration: You lie flat in the cool grass. Auntie Billow sings as she swims away from you, a note so low it buzzes in your teeth.
check_listen.prompt: Listen hard and follow where her song goes

onSuccess.narration: Her song goes out, far and low. Then it comes back from the wrong side, from behind you, as if another whale were singing back there. There is no whale back there. You sit up and look.

onFailure.narration: The song booms through the grass until your ears tickle and you giggle. You can't tell where it went. "Then go and look," says Juniper, and points her needle at the rope walk.

check_ropewalk.narration: A rope walk sways out to a bare rock at the far end of the bowl. Every plank is a different size, like a mouth full of wobbly teeth.
check_ropewalk.prompt: Cross the swaying rope walk to the far rock

onSuccess.narration: You hop across, plank by plank, and land on the far rock. From there, you see it.

onFailure.narration: A plank flips. You dangle by your hands over a great deal of sky, then haul yourself onto the far rock, scraped and puffing. From there, you see it.

check_leap.narration: Little rocks drift between the islands like stepping stones that will not sit still.
check_leap.prompt: Leap from drifting rock to drifting rock to the far end

onSuccess.narration: Hop, hop, hop. You land on the last rock, light as a cat, and see it.

onFailure.narration: A rock drifts off in the middle of your jump. You land in a bush that grows sideways out of the cliff, and climb out with leaves in your ears. From there, you see it.

check_read.narration: You look at the far end of the bowl the way only a starweaver can, past the mist, at the shape of the air itself.
check_read.prompt: Read the far sky for whatever turns the whales

onSuccess.narration: Something hangs out there. It beats like a heart, and a second heartbeat answers it from somewhere behind you, at the very same moment.

onFailure.narration: The mist swims in front of your eyes. But something out there is beating like a heart, and you point straight at it.

pair_seen.narration: Out where the whales turn, a ring of shimmer hangs in the empty sky, like heat over a summer road. It pulses: bright, dim, bright. Then Juniper gasps and points behind her own island. A second ring hangs there, close enough to throw a cake through. It pulses at the very same moment. Bright, dim, bright. Two openings, beating together like one heart. "Those weren't there in the spring," Juniper whispers.

olivia_here.narration: Beside the near opening stands Lady Olivia, the unicorn Riftseeker, mane blowing like a flag. Pip Thistledown, the young manticore scout, is at her heels, counting pulses out loud. "Ninety-one, ninety-two!" Olivia drops a feather into the near opening. A breath later, it floats out of the far one. "Linked," she says. "Two ends of one tunnel. Imagine what we could do with that." Juniper sniffs. "Feathers are not whales."

echo_test.narration: Pip holds out his spoon to you, very grandly. "Lady Olivia says a real scout tests things. Your turn!" Juniper grumbles, but she leans in to watch. How will you test the openings?

check_hum.narration: You lean close to the shimmer. It smells like rain on a hot stone, and it tickles your nose.
check_hum.prompt: Hum one long, steady note into the near opening

onSuccess.narration: Your hum goes in. A breath later it comes out of the far opening, all the way across the bowl, just as steady. Pip writes it down so fast his pencil squeaks.

onFailure.narration: Your hum cracks into a squeak. The squeak shoots out of the far opening, loud as a goose, and every whale turns to stare at you. Juniper adds a row to her scarf with a groan.

toss.narration: Pip says a pebble only goes through when the opening glows bright. Juniper says please do not hit a whale. Aim for the middle of the shimmer.

interaction.cue: Toss when the marker is in the bright middle.

onSuccess.narration: The pebble plops into the near opening and drops out of the far one, plink, into the clouds. Pip cheers.

onFailure.narration: The pebble zips through and plinks Auntie Billow on the nose. She snorts a cloud and swims wide, eyeing you all the way round.

onAssisted.narration: Pip counts the beats out loud, and the pebble goes through right on bright. Plink, out the far side.

why_circle.narration: Then Auntie Billow sings. Her song slips into the near opening and comes straight back out of the far one, ahead of her. She hears a whale singing up ahead, so she turns toward it. Now it is behind her, so she turns again. Juniper drops her needles. "She's following her own song. Round and round. Oh, poor old girl." Pip writes WHALES ARE CONFUSED, then adds AND SAD.

calf_stuck.narration: Little Hiccup has swum too close to the near opening. Each pulse tugs him in. He squeaks a worried cloud. "Quick!" says Olivia. "Lasso him with the kite lines and pull!" "Pulling frightens them," says Juniper. "Wait for the quiet beat between pulses, and sing him out." What will you do?

choices.label: Pull him free with the kite lines
Wait for the quiet beat and sing

variants.text: The other whales hang back. They still remember you.

check_haul.narration: Everyone grabs a kite line. Olivia takes the end in her teeth, which is not very ladylike. "On three!"
check_haul.prompt: Haul Hiccup out of the pull, all together

onSuccess.narration: You heave, and Hiccup pops free like a cork from a bottle.

onFailure.narration: A kite line snaps and stings your hands. Hiccup lurches, scrapes his fin on the edge of the opening, and tears free.

hauled.narration: Hiccup squeals and bolts, and the whole herd scatters after him across the sky. It takes Juniper until sunset to call them back, and they keep far away from you now. Olivia shakes out her mane. "See? Quick works." Pip writes QUICK WORKS in his notebook. Then, smaller, he writes MOSTLY.

variants.text: Hiccup has a new notch in his fin. Juniper goes very quiet. Even Olivia says, softly, "It worked. It wasn't pretty."

quiet_beat.narration: Juniper hums the whales' road song, very low. Watch the opening. In the quiet beat between pulses, the pull lets go. Sing Hiccup one long note to follow, right then and not before.

interaction.cue: Sing when the opening goes quiet.

onSuccess.narration: Your note lands in the quiet beat. Hiccup's ears lift. He turns toward you.

onFailure.narration: Your note bumps into a pulse and gets swallowed. You try again, and again.

onAssisted.narration: Juniper squeezes your hand on the quiet beat, and you sing together. Hiccup turns toward you.

check_lullaby.narration: You wait for the quiet beat, then sing low and slow, the way you would sing to a baby that is very, very large.
check_lullaby.prompt: Sing Hiccup a lullaby in the quiet beat

onSuccess.narration: Hiccup's worried squeaks slow down. He turns toward your song.

onFailure.narration: A pulse booms over your lullaby. You have to start again from the first line.

sung_out.narration: Hiccup drifts out of the pull, slow and sleepy, and rests his huge soft chin on the edge of Juniper's island. "He'll follow you now," she says. But it took ages. The sun is low, and Olivia and Pip have gone. "Off to the far opening," says Juniper. "Something about a big note. She doesn't like waiting."

sung_slow.narration: In the end Hiccup drifts free on his own, many slow pulses later. He is fine. He just doesn't know you any better than before. The sun is low, and Olivia and Pip have gone. "Off to the far opening," says Juniper. "Something about a big note. She doesn't like waiting."

choices.label: Wave Hiccup back to his auntie

olivia_offer.narration: "Here's the thing," says Lady Olivia, eyes shining. "Those openings are only half awake. That's why they pulse. Wake them all the way with one big note, and the pulsing stops. No echo, no circling. Every whale free by breakfast, and the pair wide open to the salt flats on the other side." She looks up at Billow. "She's been circling for days, Juniper. Look how tired she is."

variants.text: At sunset, Lady Olivia trots back from the far opening, Pip puffing behind her.
Pip is still staring after Hiccup, pencil in his mouth.

island_tug.narration: Then a pulse comes, bigger than all the rest. The whole island jerks toward the near opening, like a dog on a leash. The tether ropes groan. Juniper's teapot slides off its rock. "See?" says Olivia. "Half awake, and tugging. It will only get worse." How will you hold the island?

check_tether.narration: The tether ropes are as thick as your arm and wet with mist. Pip grabs the end of the line and hangs on like a sock on a washing line.
check_tether.prompt: Haul the tether ropes tight before the next pulse

onSuccess.narration: The island steadies and swings back to its place. Juniper catches her teapot in midair.

onFailure.narration: The island lurches a boat length closer before it holds. Juniper's basket of barley cakes slides over the edge and falls into the clouds. "That," she says, "was supper."

check_anchor.narration: A row of anchor stones sits by the edge, each painted with a whale. Some are heavy. Some are only heavy looking.
check_anchor.prompt: Pick the heaviest anchor stones and drop them in the right holes

onSuccess.narration: The island steadies and swings back to its place. Juniper catches her teapot in midair.

onFailure.narration: The island lurches a boat length closer before it holds. Juniper's basket of barley cakes slides over the edge and falls into the clouds. "That," she says, "was supper."

check_brace.narration: The tether post creaks and leans toward the opening. Somebody has to stand behind it and not move.
check_brace.prompt: Brace the tether post with your whole body

onSuccess.narration: The island steadies and swings back to its place. Juniper catches her teapot in midair.

onFailure.narration: The island lurches a boat length closer before it holds. Juniper's basket of barley cakes slides over the edge and falls into the clouds. "That," she says, "was supper."

juniper_answer.narration: Juniper wipes her hands on her scarf. "She's right that they're tired. And she's right that it tugs. But wake those openings that loud and the whales bolt every which way. Scattered whales stay lost for weeks, and I won't know where the island due back comes in. My way is one whale at a time, in the quiet beat." "How slow?" asks Olivia. Juniper doesn't answer.

pip_bell.narration: Pip drags a brass bell out of Olivia's pack. It is bigger than his head. "Lady Olivia needs this hung at the far opening, for the big note," he whispers. "If I do it right, she'll let me ring it!" Juniper calls from her lantern pile. "I could use a scout who can count, too." What do you tell Pip?

check_bell.narration: The bell is heavy, and the rocks out to the far opening drift. Pip steers. You carry.
check_bell.prompt: Carry the big bell across the drifting rocks and hang it

onSuccess.narration: You hang it on a crooked post beside the far opening. It hums quietly in every pulse.

onFailure.narration: A rock lurches. The bell clangs against your knee, every whale in the sky jumps, and you hang it with a bruise to show for it.

bell_hung.narration: Pip polishes the bell with his scarf until he can see his own nose in it. "Lady Olivia says one big note and they're all free," he says. "She says I can ring it." Then he looks over at Hiccup, and stops polishing. "Do whales mind loud?"

pip_lanterns.narration: Pip looks at the bell, then at Juniper, then at the bell. Then he sets it down very gently. "Lady Olivia says a good scout learns everything," he says. "That has to include lanterns." Juniper hands him one, and he holds it like a baby bird. Olivia raises one eyebrow, and hangs the bell herself.

rest.narration: Night falls. Juniper lights a fire in a ring of stones and hands out barley cakes, warm and sticky. Olivia eats hers in two bites and reads her notes by firelight. Overhead, the whales circle, singing to their own echo.

variants.text: Night falls. Juniper lights a fire in a ring of stones. The barley cakes are somewhere in the clouds, so Olivia shares her emergency oat bars. They taste a little like saddle. Overhead, the whales circle, singing to their own echo.
Hiccup sleeps with his chin on the grass beside you, snoring little clouds.
The whales circle wide, as far from your fire as they can.
Juniper casts off her scarf and starts a fresh one. "Row one," she says firmly. "I've lost count of the old one."

pip_notebook.narration: Pip's notebook has a drawing of the two openings for every night he has been here. Each night they sit a whisker further along, always the same way. "Lady Olivia says it's the wind," says Pip, chewing his pencil. "But the wind keeps changing its mind. This doesn't."

chime_lean.narration: Your Listening Chime hums in your pack. You hold it up between the two openings. It does not lean toward either one. It leans past them both, far away, back toward the glacier where all of this began. Juniper stares at it. "Something is pulling them," she whispers. "The openings. The whales. Maybe my island too." Hiccup snores a cloud, and nobody laughs.

lead_test.narration: Juniper shakes you awake before dawn. "Let's try my way once," she whispers. "Auntie Billow first. Show her the true road in the quiet beat, and she might hear it over the echo." Olivia watches from the far rock with her bell. How will you lead Auntie Billow?

choices.label: Swing lanterns in the quiet beat
Let Pip count the beats for you
Let Hiccup show her the way

variants.text: Billow keeps far off. She still remembers yesterday.
Hiccup hangs back too, his notched fin tucked in tight.

sing_road.narration: Juniper hums the whales' road song: the way her grandmother sang it. Watch the notes, then sing them back in the quiet beat.

interaction.cue: Watch the road song, then sing it back.

onSuccess.narration: Auntie Billow hears it, in the quiet beat.

onFailure.narration: Billow turns toward your song. Then the echo booms, and she turns away.

onAssisted.narration: Juniper sings each note first, and you sing it after her. Auntie Billow hears it, in the quiet beat.

sing_road_wary.narration: Billow is wary and far away, so the song has to be longer to reach her. Juniper hums every note of it. Watch, then sing them back in the quiet beat.

interaction.cue: Watch the long road song, then sing it back.

onSuccess.narration: Auntie Billow hears it, in the quiet beat.

onFailure.narration: Billow turns toward your song. Then the echo booms, and she turns away.

onAssisted.narration: Juniper sings each note first, and you sing it after her. Auntie Billow hears it, in the quiet beat.

check_lantern.narration: Juniper's lanterns hang on long poles. Swing them only in the quiet beat, so Billow sees a light where the echo isn't.
check_lantern.prompt: Swing the lanterns in the quiet beat, and only then

onSuccess.narration: Auntie Billow sees the light, in the quiet beat.

onFailure.narration: Billow turns toward the light. Then the echo booms, and she turns away.

check_lantern_pip.narration: Pip holds up his notebook and counts the pulses out loud, the way he has all week. "Bright, dim, now!"
check_lantern_pip.prompt: Swing the lanterns on Pip's count

onSuccess.narration: Auntie Billow sees the light, in the quiet beat.

onFailure.narration: Billow turns toward the light. Then the echo booms, and she turns away.

hiccup_leads.narration: Hiccup wakes, yawns a cloud, and swims up to his auntie. He bumps her gently with his nose. Then he swims out between the openings, past the echo, and waits for her in the open sky. She follows him. "He trusts you," says Juniper, "so she trusts him."

billow_out.narration: Auntie Billow stops. She listens. Then she swims straight between the two openings, past her own echo, and out into the open sky, singing. One whale. Only one. Juniper wipes her eyes on a great deal of scarf. "One," she whispers. "Eleven to go." On the far rock, Olivia says, "Lovely," and she means it.

billow_balks.narration: She tries again, and turns again. On the third try, with Juniper humming beside you, Billow slips out between the openings at last, slow and unsure. The sun is high by then. "One," says Juniper, worn out. "It works. It's just slow." On the far rock, Olivia taps her bell, not loud.

two_ways.narration: "Eleven more, at one a night," says Olivia. "Or I ring my bell, and they're all free by lunch. Scattered, yes. But free." She looks at her hooves. "When I was small, our river went the wrong way for a whole summer. Everyone waited for it to come back. It didn't. I don't like waiting." Juniper holds her scarf tight. "And I don't like losing whales."

choices.label: Juniper has a favor to ask

variants.text: Pip stands by the bell, beaming. "I hung it. Well, mostly."
Pip is still holding his lantern. He looks at it, then at Olivia, and says nothing at all.
Pip taps his notebook. "And the openings moved again last night. A whisker. Same way."

promise.narration: Juniper rolls up her scarf. "Whatever happens here, I'm going up to the lookout next, to wait for the island due back. The lookout keepers will want to know how the whales fared. Will you bring them the news yourselves? Guided or scattered, the honest way?"

promised.narration: "Honest news," says Juniper, and ties a short end of yarn around your wrist. "Show them that, and they'll know you came from me." Pip ties one around his own wrist too, though nobody asked him to.

not_promised.narration: Juniper nods. "You don't know where the next opening takes you. That's fair. I'll send a kite instead." She starts knitting the message. It is going to be a very long message.

decide.narration: The whales circle. Olivia's bell hangs ready at the far rock. Juniper's lanterns hang ready at the near one. "With all of you on the lanterns," says Juniper, "we could lead every whale out tonight. It will be a long, cold night." Olivia shrugs, not unkindly. "Or sleep on it, and choose at the openings in the morning. Mine, or hers." What will you do?

choices.label: Stay and lead the whales out
Stay and lead the whales out
Sleep on it, and choose at the openings

variants.text: Pip stands by the bell with his hand on the rope, looking at you.
Pip stands by Juniper's lanterns, his own lantern still in his paws, looking at you.

lead_night.narration: All night, you swing Juniper's lanterns in the quiet beats. One whale at a time, they hear the true road and slip out past the echo. Olivia sits on her rock and watches, chin on her hooves.
lead_night.prompt: Swing the lanterns in every quiet beat, all night long

onSuccess.narration: By the first gray light, the last tail slips out between the openings. Pip carries the brass bell back to Olivia. He never rang it.

onFailure.narration: Around midnight the lanterns dip, and three whales turn back into the echo. You start them over. The last tail slips out at noon, and you are all yawning so hard your jaws click.

hiccup_night.narration: All night, you swing Juniper's lanterns in the quiet beats, and Hiccup does the rest. He swims out past the echo, swims back, and bumps each whale with his nose until it follows him. Olivia sits on her rock and watches, chin on her hooves. "Showing off," she murmurs. By the first gray light, the last tail slips out.

guided.narration: The whales swim off into open sky, singing. Both openings stop pulsing, spread wide and hold steady, and through the far one you smell salt and mud. Olivia sighs and unhooks her bell. "Another day." Juniper sets off for the lookout, to wait for the island due back. So here is your piece: the openings come in pairs, and something keeps pulling them, the way your chime leans, back toward the glacier. Something is moving the land. What is it? And can you put things right?

variants.text: It is past noon, and every one of you is yawning.

sleep_on_it.narration: You sleep on it. Before you do, two of them come to sit by your fire, one after the other. You only have the yawns for one long talk. Who will you listen to?

olivia_night.narration: Olivia lies down by the fire, mane full of sparks. "I know you think I'm in a hurry," she says. "I am. Every night those openings move a little, and nobody knows why. If we learn to open them ourselves, then we decide where they go, not whatever is pulling them." She looks at the bell. "One note. I'm almost sure." Pip, half asleep, mumbles, "Lady Olivia is always sure."

juniper_night.narration: Juniper knits by the fire. "My grandmother's grandmother waved the island due back goodbye," she says. "We've kept a lantern lit for it ever since. When it comes home, the whales will swim ahead of it, singing, and we'll know where to stand." She pats Hiccup's chin. "If they're scattered, we'll be guessing. I'm not good at guessing."

wait_ending.narration: In the morning the whales still circle and the openings still beat together. The choice waits for you at the openings: Lady Olivia's way, quick and loud, or the whales' way, slow and quiet. Juniper sets off for the lookout, to wait for the island due back. So here is your piece: the openings come in pairs, and something keeps pulling them, the way your chime leans, back toward the glacier. Something is moving the land. What is it? And can you put things right?

variants.text: Olivia's words are still in your ears: we decide where they go.
Juniper's lantern is still in your mind, lit for an island that has not come home.
